steps: Dev-run from Terminal.app (cd PROJECT_ROOT && ./run.sh; one instance at a time — ZCode-hosted terminals get silent mic captures under macOS TCC).

Menu bar → Dictionary…: confirm the panel lists the adopted legacy terms (Qwen, MLX, Parakeet, LocalFlow, Wispr Flow, PyObjC, MacBook) and the two unapproved suggested entries (Claude, Claude Code — profile 'coding', labeled suggested).

Add a workspace-only Claude alias: canonical 'Claude', alias 'clod', scope workspace = your coding workspace's name; approve it. In the panel's Test field run 'use clod code for the cloud deployment' — expect 'use Claude Code for the cloud deployment' only after also adding the Claude Code alias, or the single-word alias result otherwise; 'cloud deployment' must never change.

Sandbox scope check pre-M06: the same alias under a workspace scope shows as suggested-but-needs-context in a global-context sandbox; live dictation applies global-scope entries only until M06 wires destination awareness (documented limitation, contracts/vocabulary.md).
Live dictation trial: dictate a sentence containing a global approved term (e.g. 'mlx') plus the words 'cloud' and 'twelve percent' — expect 'MLX', untouched 'cloud', and '12%'.
Disable the alias (panel → select entry → Disable/Enable), dictate again, confirm the behavior reverts; re-enable to restore.
Record steps, expected vs actual output, and evidence (event log lines / panel screenshots stay outside Git).

review_loop.protocol: /review-2 (two parallel read-only reviewers: bug-hunting debugger; architecture/quality/security/data-integrity auditor) then /address
critical_detail: DB1-C1: update_entry crashed on the (alias, approved) tuple format its own callers approve_entry and import_json pass — the Approve flow and alias-changing imports could never land (AttributeError before any write).
warning_detail: DB1-W1: hint_disposition semantic flip left a stale assertion in tests/v2/lifecycle/test_worker_live.py (suite not in the required list; would fail whenever run).
DB1-W2 + CA1-W1 (corroborated): aliases-only updates never bumped the entry revision column — history revisions diverged and repeated.
DB1-W3: sandbox suggestions ignored scope — the panel advertised rewrites that could not fire pre-M06.
DB1-W4: alias rows persisted the pre-update language on combined language+aliases updates.
CA1-W2: every applied hit invalidated the cached snapshot (usage inside the revision hash + meta bump) — ~120 ms main-thread rebuild per dictation at 10k-entry scale.
CA1-W3: grammar_vocabulary was O(aliases x tokens) and unmeasured on the dictation path; match_items re-sorted per normalize() call.
CA1-W4: duplicate-canonical rejections flowed through the store error channel carrying dictionary content into event detail.
CA1-W5: untested public API (delete_entry, set_scope, approve_entry, aliases-only update, 3 of 4 conflict-preview kinds) plus a vacuous immutability assertion.
addressed: Critical: update_entry/_normalize_alias_items accept str | (text, approved) tuples | Alias; regression tests for approve_entry (entry + all aliases + matching begins) and differing-alias imports.
test_worker_live assertion updated to the new disposition semantics (zero offered => nothing ignored).
Any real change (columns OR aliases) versions the entry; empty updates are no-ops that append nothing; None for non-nullable fields rejected loudly; alias rows take the updated language.
Sandbox suggestions carry in_scope + scope labels; the panel prints '(needs <scope> context active)'; suggestions never shown inside quoted literals (sandbox now uses the engine tokenizer).
record_hits no longer bumps the state counter and the snapshot revision hash excludes usage stats — an applied hit never forces a rebuild; ranking sees the last-edited snapshot (documented).

Engine matching is position-driven through a first-word alias index with the ranked order and match order precomputed at snapshot construction; the benchmark gained a normalize-with-dictionary hot-path measurement.
Duplicate-canonical probe runs on the caller thread with a content-free message; a NOCASE one-canonical-per-scope unique index backstops it; import_json keys case-insensitively.

Tests added for delete/set_scope/approve/aliases-only/language+aliases/case-variant duplicates/torn-write repair of v3 tables/real snapshot immutability/all four preview kinds/qualified-adapter request shape.
Store.submit now passes the connection (fn(db)) so _db stays module-private; the repair path re-applies all migration DDL and covers the v3 tables.
Skill-conflict records carry entry ids like alias conflicts; panel refresh/sandbox guarded with user-visible errors; on_hint_set emits a failure event instead of a silent swallow.

One address-loop fix of our own: a scoped-retrieval benchmark run crossed the 25 ms gate (25.3 ms) on machine noise — fixed structurally by precomputing ranking at snapshot construction (5.3 ms p95 after).
deferred: Deep-freezing HintSet.scope/conflicts/omitted containers (to_json copies on read; all consumers in-repo — discipline documented in contracts/vocabulary.md).
A single shared edge-punctuation helper across engine/vocabulary (the sandbox now uses the engine tokenizer outright; the two grammar sites share the same inline constant — cosmetic dedup only).

Selector ranking freshness: recency/frequency see the last-edited snapshot because usage no longer invalidates it (trade-off taken deliberately to keep hits off the rebuild path; recorded in contracts/vocabulary.md).
review_loop.post_address_verification: All 21 automated suites + test_worker_live + both model-backed suites re-run green; benchmark re-run on the fixed code with all gates passing.

privacy: Committed artifacts carry synthetic fixtures, hashes and counts only; the envelope's context/vocabulary blocks carry ids, revisions and counts (no terms — the frozen hint set's terms live in a lease-governed store artifact); duplicate-rejection events carry no dictionary content; the baseline-manifest privacy scan passes over every new path; the store error channel never sees canonical spellings.
